cover.alt: Tansy and the Parrot Family on a red picnic blanket by the gold tree, as a big bubble floats toward Tansy’s sandwich

text: Tansy was busy. She had ten acorns to bury before lunch.
She dug a hole. She dropped in an acorn. She drew a map on bark, so she could find it again.
Then the sky got loud, very, very loud.
“SQUAWK! SQUAWK! SQUAWK!”
Three parrots were coming in to land by her tree.

media.alt: Tansy digs a hole by her tree as the three parrots swoop down from the sky

text: June the mom landed first. Johnafur the dad landed next. Baby Juneafur landed last, with her bubble blower in her wing.
“We have a plan for the day!” sang June.
“A plan for the day, with food on a tray!” sang Johnafur.
“A nicpic!” sang Juneafur. “A nicpic! Hooray!”
“She means a picnic,” said June. “Will you come, Tansy?”

media.alt: The Parrot Family stands in front of Tansy by her tree, singing their invite

text: “Yes! Yes! YES!” said Tansy, all in one breath. “When is it? Where is it? What is there to eat?”
“On the hill, by our gold tree,” said June.
“At noon, at noon! Come soon, come soon!” sang Johnafur.
Tansy was so happy, she hopped up and down. She forgot her acorns. She forgot her map. It blew off in the wind.

media.alt: Tansy hops for joy while her bark map blows away and the parrots cheer

text: At dusk, Tansy sat down to make a plan. Her plans always came in steps.
Step one: Go up the hill to the gold tree.
Step two: Eat a jam sandwich.
Step three: Eat a cupcake with pink frosting.
Step four: Eat all the rest.
It was the best plan she ever had. It was also the shortest.
She went to bed with a big grin. She did not know what was coming.

media.alt: At dusk, Tansy sits by her tree with her plan scratched on a piece of bark

text: At noon, Tansy ran up the hill. There was the gold tree. Its leaves shone like coins.
In the trunk was a tiny door. It was as small as a nut.
Then the door began to grow. It grew and grew. Now it was as big as three parrots.
Out came June, Johnafur and Juneafur, with a big basket.

media.alt: The Parrot Family steps out of the door in their gold tree with a picnic basket as Tansy runs up

text: Johnafur spread out a red blanket. June set out the food.
There was a tall stack of bread and jam. There was a bunch of green grapes. There was a big block of cheese. And there were six cupcakes with pink frosting.
“Not too close to the edge, Juneafur!” said June. “Sit by me.”
“Sit by me, sit by me!” sang Juneafur. Then she sat by Tansy.

media.alt: A red picnic blanket full of sandwiches, grapes, cheese and pink cupcakes, with Tansy and the parrots around it

text: Tansy picked up a sandwich. “Step two,” she said. She opened wide.
Just then, Juneafur’s bubble blower went PFFT.
Out came a bubble, big and shiny. It floated up, up, up… and landed on Tansy’s nose.
POP!

media.alt: A big shiny bubble pops on Tansy’s nose just as she lifts a sandwich

text: “A-A-A-CHOO!” Tansy let out a huge sneeze.
The sandwich flew out of her paw. It went up in the air. It came down on Johnafur’s head.
Now he had a sandwich hat. Jam ran down his beak.
“A hat, a hat, a jam sandwich hat!” sang June.
“A hat, a hat! I like that!” sang Johnafur.
“Okay,” said Tansy. “That bite did not count.”

media.alt: Tansy sneezes and her sandwich lands on Johnafur’s head like a hat

text: Tansy picked up the cheese. “Step two,” she said again. She opened wide.
Just then, Puddle the duck came up the hill.
Puddle was not looking at the picnic. He was looking at a moth.
The moth flew over the blanket. So Puddle walked over the blanket too.

media.alt: Puddle the duck walks onto the picnic blanket, staring up at a moth

text: SQUISH went the grapes. SPLAT went a cupcake. PLOP! Puddle sat down on the cheese.
“Oh, hello,” said Puddle. “Is this a picnic? What was I doing?”
Then he got up and walked off. The cheese was stuck to his tail feathers.
“Bye, cheese,” said Tansy sadly.
“Bye, bye, cheese!” sang Juneafur, with a wave of her wing.

media.alt: Puddle walks away with the block of cheese stuck to his tail while Tansy watches

text: Moss the hedgehog was hiding in a bush. He was too shy to come out.
“Come and sit, come and sit!” sang June. “There is still lots to eat!”
Moss came out very slowly. He sat on the very edge of the blanket.
Tansy picked up a cupcake. “Step THREE,” she said. “I will skip step two.” She opened wide.

media.alt: Shy Moss sits at the edge of the blanket while Tansy holds up a pink cupcake

text: Just then, PFFT! went the bubble blower. A bubble floated over to Moss. POP! It went off by his ear.
Moss did what Moss always does. He rolled into a ball.
And the hill was very, very steep.
Moss rolled down. He rolled over the grapes. He rolled over the cupcakes. He rolled over Tansy’s tail.

media.alt: Moss, rolled into a ball, tumbles down the hill across the picnic

text: At the bottom of the hill, Moss stopped. Green grapes were stuck to each of his spikes.
On top sat Tansy’s cupcake, like a pink hat.
“Sorry,” came a small squeak from inside. “I think I am a grape now.”
Tansy looked down at her paw. It was empty.
“More hats!” sang Juneafur. “Hats, hats, hats!”

media.alt: At the bottom of the hill, Moss is a ball covered in green grapes with a pink cupcake on top

text: Tansy was very, very hungry now. Her tummy went GRRR.
So she made a new plan.
Step one: No bubbles at all.
Step two: No ducks on the blanket.
Step three: No more rolling hedgehogs.
Step four: EAT.
Juneafur hid her bubble blower under her wing. June held Juneafur. Johnafur held his breath.

media.alt: Tansy holds her new bark plan while the parrots sit very, very still

text: There was just one sandwich left. Tansy held it up. No one made a peep.
She opened wide…
“BREAKING NEWS! BREAKING NEWS!”
Wren zoomed in from the sky. She landed on the sandwich, feet first, in the jam.
“A giant is coming up the hill!” sang Wren. “A big, big giant, with a big, big bucket!”

media.alt: Wren zooms down and lands feet first on Tansy’s last sandwich

text: Tansy did not hear the news. She had seen something in the grass.
It was an acorn, a fat and shiny acorn.
Tansy dropped the sandwich. She dug a hole. She hid the acorn. She drew a map on a bit of bark.
“There,” she said. “Now, where was I?”
She looked for her sandwich. Ten little ants were taking it down the hill.

media.alt: Tansy buries an acorn while a line of ants carries her last sandwich down the hill

text: “Bye, sandwich,” said Tansy softly.
She sat down on the messy blanket. There was no bread, no cheese and no grapes. The grapes were all on Moss.
“This is the worst picnic,” she said.
Then she looked at Johnafur. He still had jam on his head. Moss was still a grape.
Tansy’s lip went wobbly. Then out came a snort, then a laugh, then a BIG laugh.
The parrots laughed too. Moss laughed so hard, three grapes fell off.

media.alt: Tansy, the parrots and grape-covered Moss laugh together on the messy blanket

text: THUMP, THUMP, THUMP. Big boots were coming up the hill.
It was the giant! She had a bucket in her hand. She was humming a song.
The whole picnic held still. Moss held the most still of all. He had lots of practice.

media.alt: Zoe walks up the hill with her bucket while the animals freeze on the blanket

text: The giant looked at the messy blanket. She looked at the grape hedgehog. She looked at the parrot with jam on his head.
“Looks like someone had a picnic!” she said, with a laugh.
Then she tipped her bucket. Out came nuts and seeds and carrots. Out came a big pile of berries.
“Here you go, little friends,” said the giant. “Lunch is on me.”

media.alt: Zoe tips her bucket of nuts, seeds, carrots and berries onto the picnic blanket

text: “What did the giant say?” said June.
“She said, ‘Looks like someone had a PIG-nic!’” said Wren. That was not what she said. But it was close.
Tansy picked up a nut. She looked up and she looked down. There were no bubbles, no ducks, no news and no acorns.
She took a big bite. CRUNCH!
“Step two,” said Tansy, with her mouth full. “At last!”

media.alt: Tansy finally bites a nut while Wren tells the parrots what the giant said

text: They all ate and ate. The giant stood in the grass and hummed.
Then Juneafur blew one tiny bubble. It floated up, up, up… and landed on the giant’s cheek.
POP!
The giant laughed, and so did the whole picnic.
“Best nicpic ever!” said Juneafur.
And this time, no one fixed the word. It was just the best.

media.alt: Zoe laughs as a tiny bubble from Juneafur lands on her cheek, with all the animals eating around her
